name: Expert parallelism for MoE: when EP beats TP and the dispatch/combine overhead
arithmetic_intensity: EP shards experts across GPUs rather than sharding each expert's weights. For a MoE model with E experts, EP assigns E/N experts to each GPU. The arithmetic intensity of each expert GEMM is the same as a dense GEMM at the same batch size, but the batch is split across experts by the router. The key advantage over TP: EP requires no all-reduce per layer (only an all-to-all dispatch and combine), so the communication cost is O(B*d) rather than O(B*d*N). The key disadvantage: load imbalance - if the router sends more tokens to some experts than others, some GPUs idle while others are saturated. DeepSeek-V3 uses 256 experts with top-8 routing, and the report discusses EP as the preferred parallelism strategy for MoE models.
scales_with: num_experts (more experts = more parallelism but also more dispatch overhead)
top_k_routing (higher k = more tokens per expert = better load balance but more communication)
expert_capacity_factor (the maximum tokens per expert before overflow)
num_gpus (EP degree determines how many experts per GPU)
workarounds: Expert parallelism (EP): shard experts across GPUs, avoiding per-layer all-reduce
DeepSeek-V3's 256 experts with top-8 routing: uses EP as the preferred parallelism strategy
Expert capacity factor: cap tokens per expert to prevent overflow
Auxiliary-loss-free load balancing: DeepSeek-V3's approach to balance expert load without auxiliary loss
Combine EP with TP: use EP across nodes and TP within nodes for large MoE models
notes: When EP beats TP: for MoE models with many experts, EP is preferred because (1) it avoids the per-layer all-reduce that TP requires, (2) it scales naturally with the number of experts, and (3) the all-to-all dispatch/combine is cheaper than N all-reduces for large N. When TP beats TP: for dense models or MoE with few experts, TP is simpler and has lower overhead. The crossover depends on the number of experts and the batch size. DeepSeek-V3's 256 experts with top-8 routing means each token is processed by 8 experts, so the effective batch per expert is B*8/E = B*8/256 = B/32. For B=128, each expert sees 4 tokens on average, which is too few for efficient GEMM. This is why MoE models need large batch sizes or expert capacity factors to utilize GPUs efficiently. The dispatch/combine overhead is the price of EP: each token must be routed to its top-k experts, and the results must be combined. This is O(B*k*d) communication, which is cheaper than TP's O(B*d*N) for large N but still significant.
